b-intro-01.title: Your first query
b-intro-01.description: Return **all columns** and all rows of the `customers` table.
hints: The `*` symbol in SELECT means "all columns".
b-intro-01.explanation: `SELECT *` returns every column, and the absence of `WHERE` returns every row of the table.

b-intro-02.title: Product names
b-intro-02.description: Return only the names (`name`) of all products from the `products` table.
hints: List the column you need after SELECT.
b-intro-02.explanation: To get a single column, it is enough to put its name after `SELECT`.

b-intro-03.title: Read the query
hints: There is no WHERE and no LIMIT in the query, so rows are not filtered.
b-intro-03.explanation: The query selects two columns from every row of the `customers` table. There is no filtering, so every customer is returned, including those whose city is NULL.
options: Returns the name and city of every customer
Returns only customers whose city is known
Creates a new table with names and cities
Returns only the first customer in the table

b-intro-04.title: All order columns
b-intro-04.description: Which query returns **all columns** of the `orders` table?
hints: A query always starts with SELECT and contains FROM.
b-intro-04.explanation: The correct syntax is `SELECT * FROM orders`. There is no `GET` command in SQL, and `SELECT orders` tries to select a column that does not exist.

b-intro-05.title: How many categories?
b-intro-05.description: How many rows will this query return? Look at the `categories` table in the "Schema" tab.
hints: Without WHERE a query returns every row of the table.
b-intro-05.explanation: The `categories` table has 10 rows, and a query without a filter returns all of them.

b-intro-06.title: Query keywords
b-intro-06.description: Fill in the missing keywords to get the name and price of every product.
hints: The first word says "select", the second one says "from the table".
b-intro-06.explanation: The basic query structure is `SELECT columns FROM table`.

b-intro-07.title: Assemble the query
b-intro-07.description: Arrange the fragments to get the title and release year of every movie.
hints: A query starts with SELECT, then the columns, then FROM and the table.
b-intro-07.explanation: The order of query parts is fixed: `SELECT` → column list → `FROM` → table.

b-intro-08.title: Directors
b-intro-08.description: Return the name (`name`) and country (`country`) of every director from the `directors` table.
b-intro-08.explanation: Columns in `SELECT` are separated by commas and returned in the listed order.

b-intro-09.title: A typo
b-intro-09.description: The query should return the names of all products, but it fails with an error. Fix it.
hints: Read the error message: the database points to the place where the query stopped making sense.
b-intro-09.explanation: The keyword must be spelled exactly: `SELECT`. A "syntax error" almost always means a typo or a missing character.
